The post NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B Open Multimodal Agent Model appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> NVIDIA just released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL , an open vision-language model built for always-on enterprise agents. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model from NVIDIA that activates 12B parameters per token. It reads text, images, documents and video, then reasons, calls tools and writes code in one model. For developers, 1 open checkpoint replaces a separate text model along with a separate vision model. NVIDIA also shipped 2 edge models, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B and Bolt E4B. TL;DR Size: 120B total parameters, 12B active (MoE). Context up to 1M tokens. Runs on: 1x DGX Spark, 1x H200, 2x H100 or 1x GB200 with the NVFP4 checkpoint. A BF16 checkpoint is also published. Performance: Strong reasoning, agentic coding and document vision. NVIDIA claims up to 5x higher single-GPU throughput than open peers. Best: 89.90 on GPQA-Diamond (NVFP4). Worst: 17.78 on tau3-bench banking (NVFP4). What is Nemotron 3.5 Super VL? It is an open multimodal agent model. Weights ship under the OpenMDW-1.1 license . NVIDIA also released open datasets , training recipes and RL environments in NeMo Gym. The model card lists text, image and video inputs with text output. Video is limited to MP4 clips up to 2 minutes. Reasoning can be toggled on or off through the chat template. How does the architecture work? The backbone interleaves Mamba-2, mixture-of-experts and attention layers. Each MoE layer holds 512 routed experts. A C-RADIO vision encoder and a connector feed images, document pages and video frames into the language backbone. Speed comes from four techniques: Multi-token prediction: a native drafter proposes several tokens, verified in 1 forward pass. LiLiCorr: a speculative drafter for DGX Spark, up to 2.3x faster token generation. NVFP4 with quantization-aware distillation: 4-bit weights and activations on Blackwell, 4-bit weights with 16-bit activations elsewhere. Context reuse: prefix caching keeps both attention caches and Mamba states across agent turns. The model was distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra. NVIDIA team states that it trained on about 26 trillion tokens. Post-training used roughly 3.8 million samples plus RL across dozens of environments. Continued pretraining added 10B Indic tokens. How does it perform on benchmarks? All scores below are NVIDIA-reported, from the NVFP4 checkpoint on the model card. Area Benchmark Score Reasoning GPQA-Diamond 89.90 Coding SWE-bench Verified 71.07 Coding Terminal-Bench 2.1 60.80 Web agent BrowseComp 77.5 Instruction following IFBench 71.50 Charts CharXiv reasoning 79.88 Documents MMLongBench-Doc 62.82 Computer use OSWorld-Verified 52.3 Long-horizon agent tau3-bench banking 17.78 On agent harness evals, Super VL beats Nemotron 3 Ultra. The Liquid AI d1-ultra decision model reads text, images, or both. It answers typed questions with a probability for each possible answer. It does this in one forward pass and generates no output tokens. For developers, that means classification, routing and scoring calls without paying for generated text. It is available now on the Liquid API at $0.042 per million input tokens. TL;DR Size: Parameters and context length not disclosed. Built on a larger open-weight backbone than d1. Runs on: Hosted Liquid API only. No downloadable weights or quantized variants announced. Performance: Leads all 8 categories in Liquid’s 112-evaluation suite, per Liquid. Best: 65 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index, ranked #1 (Liquid-reported). Worst: No public per-benchmark breakdown or parameter count yet; claims are vendor-reported. What is a decision model? A decision model answers bounded questions with probabilities instead of free text. Liquid’s decision model docs describe 3 question types: Noul: a yes/no question that returns a probability between 0 and 1. Choice: one label from a set, with a probability per label. Score: a probability-weighted position on an ordered rubric. The docs recommend decision models for routing, moderation, guardrails, triage and LLM-as-judge replacement. They recommend a language model for summarization, chat and code generation. How does d1-ultra work? Each request carries a state (the context), optional images , and 1 or more typed questions . The model evaluates every question against the same input in 1 call. The d1 API reference shows responses with output_tokens always at 0. Liquid AI team states that d1-ultra uses a larger open-weight backbone than d1 , along with heavy Liquid-specific customizations. Combined with Liquid’s decision training pipeline, the gains are largest on knowledge tasks. Liquid AI team built d1-ultra for messy cases. Its examples include spotting a circuit board defect against a spec. Another is checking a damage claim against the customer’s photo. How does d1-ultra perform on benchmarks? Liquid AI compared d1-ultra against its earlier d1 and TypeSafe’s Jev 1.14 across 112 evaluations. According to Liquid AI’s announcement , d1-ultra outperforms Jev 1.14 across all tasks at the same price. On the independent Artificial Analysis Decision Index , Liquid reports d1-ultra ranks #1 with a score of 65. The index averages 4 evaluations at 25% each: AA-Omniscience-Decision: knowledge and hallucination HLE-MultiChoice: reasoning When2Call: tool calling WildGuardTest: safety classification For context, Artificial Analysis’s Oct 13 launch article listed Jev 1.13 first at 58. GLiDE and Microsoft-Decision-1 followed at 54 each. Liquid says Vercel AI Gateway and OpenRouter support is coming soon. You can test it first in the d1 Playground . Billing covers input tokens only. Per Liquid’s pricing notes , images cost 1.5 tokens per 32×32-pixel patch. A 1024×1024 image therefore costs 1,536 tokens. Each question is billed as its own prompt, including its text and all images. So 3 questions on 1 image bill that image 3 times. The endpoint docs cap requests at 8 images and 10,000 image patches.
